paragraphs: A navigation agent must connect written instructions with a changing stream of visual observations. Reasoning can help it keep track of progress and choose appropriate actions, but invoking reasoning at fixed intervals can waste computation or miss difficult decisions. AdaNav makes the timing of reasoning something the agent learns to control.

Its central component is a lightweight block that decides when to trigger reasoning based on uncertainty. The authors use action entropy, which reflects uncertainty across possible actions, as an initial guide. A training procedure then moves from heuristic guidance toward reinforcement learning, refining when the agent should spend effort reasoning. This approach targets the limited training data available for embodied tasks.

With 6,000 training samples, the authors report success-rate improvements over closed-source models trained on millions of examples: 20% on R2R val-unseen, 11.7% on RxR-CE, and 11.4% in real-world scenes. These findings support adapting reasoning to decision difficulty as a useful way to improve navigation under limited-data conditions.
icml-2026-adanav-adaptive-reasoning-with.tldr: AdaNav learns when uncertainty warrants extra reasoning, improving instruction-following navigation with 6,000 training samples.

paragraphs: Protein structure tokenizers turn structural information into sequences that models can process. Existing approaches build tokens from local neighborhoods, which can limit both generation and representation learning. This paper instead introduces global tokenization: successive tokens add progressively finer detail to a representation of the whole protein structure.

The global organization mitigates error accumulation during generation and produces embeddings without requiring a separate operation to reduce a sequence into a representation. It also lets the information content of the token sequence adapt to the task. The authors use this flexibility to support inference criteria based on how much information generated proteins contain.

Across reconstruction, generation, and representation tasks, the method matches or exceeds models using local structure tokenizers. On CATH classification tasks, nonlinear probes applied to its token sequences outperform equivalent probes using other tokenizers. The paper also demonstrates zero-shot protein shrinking and affinity maturation. Together, these results show how changing the unit of structural encoding can support both useful representations and more adaptable protein generation.
icml-2026-adaptive-protein-tokenization-.tldr: A global protein tokenizer adds structural detail progressively, supporting adaptive generation and strong protein representations.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-experts models use computation efficiently, but storing and running their experts can still be expensive. Compression methods often rank or remove whole experts. The paper argues that this level of decision is too coarse, particularly when experts differ substantially and the model dynamically routes inputs among them.

The authors observe that information within an expert is concentrated in a small number of channels. Consequently, even an expert judged important overall can contain considerable redundancy. Their structural pruning framework uses an efficient attribution-based approximation to score channels and formulates pruning around maximizing coverage of those scores. This gives compression decisions access to differences within experts, beyond an overall expert ranking.

Experiments on DeepSeek and Qwen models report retained accuracy with 50% or 25% pruning combined with 4-bit quantization. The reported memory reduction for Qwen3-30B-A3B is 5.27 times, and the method outperforms leading baselines across the evaluated benchmarks. These findings support channel-level attribution as a useful basis for compressing models whose experts contain unevenly distributed information.
icml-2026-attribution-guided-and-coverag.tldr: Channel-level attribution guides MoE pruning, preserving useful information while substantially reducing memory alongside quantization.

paragraphs: LoRA adapts a model using a small set of trainable parameters, but its performance depends on how adaptation capacity is distributed across modules. Giving every module the same rank ignores their different needs. Methods that adjust this allocation can introduce training overhead or require new planning for each configuration.

CSPLoRA separates structural planning from subsequent adaptation. During a probe, it reweights examples according to prediction uncertainty to estimate module importance. Its motivating insight is that examples the model struggles with provide more informative gradients for identifying important modules than easy examples. Those estimates become structural priors for assigning the available rank budget.

For a fixed task and model, the resulting plan can be reused across compatible rank budgets and LoRA backends. Experiments on GLUE, commonsense reasoning, and arithmetic show average improvements over uniform LoRA with comparable parameter counts, including a 1.25-point gain on LLaMA-2-7B commonsense reasoning. The practical contribution is a reusable planning step whose applicability remains tied to compatible configurations of the same task-model pair.
icml-2026-csplora-confidence-guided-stru.tldr: CSPLoRA uses uncertain examples to plan reusable LoRA rank allocations that improve average performance with comparable parameter counts.

paragraphs: A support vector machine seeks a decision boundary with a wide separating margin, while a deep network learns the features used for classification. Typical hybrid approaches place an SVM on features treated as fixed inputs, leaving its margin geometry unable to guide the feature extractor. DDSVM connects these two parts through repeated updates.

The framework alternates between fitting a linear SVM to normalized features and updating the neural backbone using directions defined by the SVM margin. The current boundary therefore becomes a changing teacher for representation learning. As features change, the SVM is fitted again, allowing the boundary and representation to influence each other throughout optimization.

Normalizing feature lengths places them on a sphere. Under this normalization, the resulting feature gradient lies along the sphere's tangent space, so optimization targets angular separation. On image-classification benchmarks with scarce data, DDSVM reports top-1 error reductions of 5.6–8.3%. The findings support using explicit margin geometry to shape learned representations in the evaluated limited-data settings.
icml-2026-ddsvm-a-differentiable-framewo.tldr: DDSVM repeatedly feeds SVM margin geometry back into a neural feature extractor, reducing classification error under data scarcity.

paragraphs: Clustering an attributed graph requires combining information about individual nodes with information about their connections. Noisy edges can spread misleading information, while overlapping feature representations can add redundancy. This paper addresses both problems through a self-supervised method that reconstructs graph connections and reduces redundancy between two learned views.

To reconstruct topology, the method intersects nearest-neighbor relationships with the original adjacency relationships. It also uses global information from K-means clustering to filter noisy nodes. These steps refine the structure used for graph-based feature aggregation. The goal is to make the information passed between nodes more useful for separating clusters.

The two feature views come naturally from an autoencoder and a graph autoencoder. Mutual-information minimization and a decorrelation constraint suppress redundant information between them, encouraging more discriminative representations. Across ACM, DBLP, CITE, and AMAP, the method consistently outperforms six leading baselines. The results support jointly improving the graph used for aggregation and the complementarity of the representations used for clustering.
icml-2026-discriminative-attribute-graph.tldr: Reconstructing graph connections and reducing redundancy between feature views improves clustering across four evaluated graph datasets.

paragraphs: Electronic health records contain many diseases that share risk factors, including rare outcomes that are difficult to estimate. Treating each disease separately can miss this shared structure. The paper introduces a Bayesian framework that organizes disease risk around latent pathways, making both disease groupings and risk-factor influences explicit objects of inference.

Each pathway is represented by a hyperedge: a group that can contain several diseases. A disease can belong to multiple pathways, and risk factors influence risk at the pathway level. This captures higher-order patterns beyond pairs of diseases. A repulsion prior encourages a compact, identifiable structure, while posterior inference quantifies uncertainty about pathway membership and risk-factor effects.

For large datasets, a structured variational algorithm preserves dependencies among whether a pathway exists, which diseases belong to it, and its effects. Experiments on simulated data and UK Biobank show stable, interpretable pathways, well-calibrated uncertainty, improved estimates for rare diseases, and competitive prediction. The findings support shared pathway modeling as a way to combine predictive usefulness with interpretable risk structure.
icml-2026-disentangling-latent-risk-path.tldr: Bayesian hypergraph inference models overlapping disease-risk pathways, improving rare-disease estimation while quantifying uncertainty.

paragraphs: Data cleaning changes what a model can learn, while model construction determines how effectively cleaned data is used. Running cleaning and automated model selection as separate stages can spend a limited budget inefficiently. DMCO treats the two activities as a joint optimization problem with an explicit resource limit.

The framework divides work into time slices and adaptively interleaves cleaning with AutoML. Its gradient-based cleaning sampling strategy has theoretical guarantees for minimizing gradient-estimation variance. It combines this strategy with loss-driven sampling and progressive model fitting, allowing model construction to benefit from intermediate improvements in data quality as the process continues.

On six real-world datasets, DMCO consistently outperforms standalone cleaning and AutoML baselines on classification and regression, measured with F1 and mean squared error. Under limited budgets, it reaches up to 82.19% of the performance of full cleaning followed by exhaustive AutoML and remains robust across different AutoML frameworks. The result supports coordinating cleaning and model search as computation is spent, rather than treating their interaction as a one-time handoff.
icml-2026-dmco-budget-aware-co-optimizat.tldr: DMCO adaptively interleaves data cleaning and AutoML to improve predictive performance within a fixed computational budget.

paragraphs: Outlier detection is difficult to configure for a new dataset when labeled anomalies are unavailable. Without those labels, selecting an algorithm and its settings becomes challenging. OUTFORMER addresses this deployment problem with a foundation model pretrained to perform tabular outlier detection using examples supplied directly in its input context.

The method advances FOMO-0D through a mixture of synthetic priors and a self-evolving training curriculum. Pretraining uses only synthetic labeled datasets. For a new task, the model takes that task's training data as context and predicts labels for test examples through a forward pass. This requires no labeled outliers, additional outlier-model training, or bespoke model selection at deployment.

The authors report state-of-the-art performance on ADBench and on two newly introduced large-scale outlier-detection benchmarks comprising more than 1,500 datasets, while retaining fast inference. These findings support synthetic pretraining and in-context learning as a practical combination for transferring outlier detection to new tasks. Here, zero-shot deployment still uses the new task's data as context.
icml-2026-from-zero-to-hero-advancing-ze.tldr: OUTFORMER uses synthetic pretraining and in-context learning for fast tabular outlier detection without task-specific training or labeled outliers.

paragraphs: Dynamic Gaussian splatting represents changing scenes explicitly and can produce high-quality rendered views. The authors find that generalization can deteriorate when scenes contain large motion. They investigate optimization as a source of this problem and introduce a mixture of update strategies for two representative open-source explicit dynamic-splatting pipelines.

The method has three components. Space- and time-dependent sparse updates include additional regularization to stabilize adaptive optimization. A constant-corrected adaptive algorithm reduces excessive scaling of gradients for Gaussian primitives and combines adaptive with non-adaptive steps. Stochastic Attribute Averaging mixes primitive attributes to reduce frame preference, where optimization favors particular frames under motion disturbances.

Experiments show consistent improvements and fewer generalization problems in the studied pipelines. The findings highlight the contribution of non-adaptive updates and the influence of frame preference when optimizing explicit dynamic scene representations. The paper therefore connects rendering generalization under motion to how primitive parameters are updated, showing that changes to optimization can improve these existing representations.
icml-2026-improving-explicit-dynamic-gau.tldr: Mixing sparse, adaptive, non-adaptive, and averaged updates improves generalization in two explicit dynamic Gaussian-splatting pipelines.

paragraphs: LoRA makes adaptation economical by learning updates within a low-dimensional parameter space. This paper argues that its usual parameterization may explore that space insufficiently and that flattening convolutional tensors into matrices can degrade performance. LAVA develops a unified parameterization for adapting both language-model matrices and vision-model convolution kernels.

The authors empirically verify low-rank subspaces in convolutional layers, then express parameter changes as sums of learnable rank-one components. This gives matrices and convolution kernels a shared adaptation framework. They also analyze LoRA's optimization dynamics and add orthogonal regularization, providing a theoretical result that this regularization helps reduce gradient variance and thereby supports training stability.

Reported experiments favor LAVA across downstream tasks. For LLaMA2-7b commonsense tasks, performance is 1.9% higher than LoRA. In metric depth estimation, LAVA trains about 1.5% of the parameters of Depth-Anything's 335.3-million-parameter model and improves delta-one accuracy by 3.5% over LoRA and 5.6% over SVDiff. These results support the proposed parameterization across both matrix-based and convolutional adaptation.
icml-2026-lava-a-unified-framework-for-f.tldr: LAVA adapts language and vision models through learnable rank-one components, with orthogonal regularization to reduce gradient variance.

paragraphs: A 3D scene graph represents objects as nodes and their relationships as edges. Generating these graphs from RGB-D sequences requires distinguishing categories that can look similar while accommodating substantial variation within each category. GMPSSG addresses these category-level issues alongside the extraction of object and relationship features.

The framework assigns each category its own prototype represented by a Gaussian mixture. Separate category prototypes help reduce confusion between categories, while multiple components within a prototype represent diversity inside one category. Prototype-anchored representation learning organizes the feature space around these category structures, aiming to make the categories distinct and internally expressive.

A topology-aware interaction mechanism then uses implicit co-occurrence patterns in the scene to adjust prototype distributions. This helps align object and relationship predictions into plausible node-edge combinations. On the 3DSSG dataset, GMPSSG outperforms several leading methods. The findings support combining flexible category representations with scene-level relational information, so predictions account for both what an individual feature resembles and how it fits the surrounding graph.
icml-2026-learning-gaussian-mixture-dist.tldr: GMPSSG uses Gaussian-mixture category prototypes and scene co-occurrence patterns to improve 3D object-and-relation graph generation.

paragraphs: Vision-language models need examples of successful self-correction to learn how to revise faulty reasoning. During reinforcement learning, these behaviors occur rarely, leaving a sparse training signal. Octopus addresses this shortage by constructing correction-focused supervision from rollouts the training process has already produced.

The framework recombines existing rollouts to create denser self-correction examples without the computational overhead reported for generating additional material. This augmentation improves sample efficiency and stabilizes optimization. The authors also separate learning to self-correct from learning to reason directly through a two-stage reinforcement-learning strategy. Separating these objectives is intended to avoid conflicts between their training signals.

The resulting Octopus-8B model has controllable self-correction capabilities. The authors report state-of-the-art performance among open-source vision-language models across seven benchmarks, exceeding the best reinforcement-learning-from-verifiable-rewards baseline by 1.0 score while using 0.72 times its training time per step. The findings suggest that organizing existing training trajectories into useful correction examples can make self-correction easier to learn while also improving training efficiency.
icml-2026-learning-self-correction-in-vi.tldr: Octopus recombines existing rollouts and separates training stages to teach vision-language self-correction more efficiently.

paragraphs: Bowel sounds offer a non-invasive way to assess gastrointestinal movement, but speech interference can overlap with their frequencies. Clinical noise can also contain abrupt, unusually large disturbances that Gaussian-based diffusion methods struggle to model. This paper develops a Cauchy-driven diffusion bridge to recover bowel sounds from such interference.

The authors introduce ClinBS, a clinical dataset containing more than 25 hours of recordings and expert-verified rare pathological transients. Their mathematical formulation uses a Cauchy driver to better represent heavy-tailed noise and derives closed-form density and score expressions. An efficient sampling procedure represents the noise through a Gaussian scale mixture, making the proposed restoration process practical to execute.

Experiments report state-of-the-art results, with improvements of 13.4%–49.8% over baselines across the core metrics and abnormal bowel-sound recognition accuracy reaching 88.01%. These findings connect better noise modeling with both signal restoration and recognition of abnormal sounds. They support the system's potential for gastrointestinal monitoring and diagnosis, as stated by the authors.
icml-2026-listening-through-the-noise-ca.tldr: A Cauchy-driven diffusion bridge restores bowel sounds amid heavy-tailed interference and improves abnormal-sound recognition.

paragraphs: Representing moving 3D content requires preserving both spatial structure and change over time. Existing 4D variational autoencoders often rely on projected 2D pointmaps, which provide incomplete, viewpoint-dependent observations. The paper argues that these projections can distort structure and irreversibly displace tokens from their proper spatial and temporal relationships.

The proposed autoencoder works directly with dynamic colored voxels in native 4D space. Its encoder and decoder retain explicit spatial and temporal coordinates, allowing it to encode both partial and complete content. Attention operates within local 4D windows to support flexible temporal compression. A differentiable rendering loss based on sparse voxel rasterization further improves geometry and color reconstruction.

On 4D reconstruction tasks, the method achieves higher fidelity than pointmap and flow-based autoencoders while learning a more structurally consistent latent space. The authors also train a video-conditioned 4D diffusion model to demonstrate generative potential. The contribution is a representation that keeps space and time explicit throughout compression and reconstruction, with benefits shown for reconstruction and an initial generative application.
icml-2026-native-spatio-temporal-4d-vari.tldr: A native 4D voxel autoencoder preserves spatial and temporal coordinates, improving reconstruction and supporting video-conditioned generation.

paragraphs: Multi-task learning can improve estimation by letting related tasks share a representation while retaining their own parameters. Even with a linear shared representation, jointly learning these pieces produces a non-convex matrix-factorization problem. The paper addresses whether likelihood-based methods can solve this problem efficiently with strong statistical guarantees.

The authors introduce a first-order algorithm that learns the shared representation and task-specific parameters together. They establish a convergence bound of approximately constant iterations with logarithmic factors suppressed. Its estimation error scales as dk divided by TN, again up to logarithmic factors, where d is input dimension, k is representation dimension, T is the number of tasks, and N is the number of samples per task.

The reported error is near-optimal and improves on existing likelihood-based methods by a factor of k. The bound makes the value of shared data explicit: more tasks and more samples per task improve estimation relative to the dimensions being learned. The result establishes computational and statistical efficiency for the studied shared-linear-representation problem.
icml-2026-near-optimal-and-efficient-fir.tldr: A first-order likelihood-based algorithm jointly learns shared linear representations and task parameters with near-optimal estimation error.

paragraphs: Writing a small function or repairing an existing repository tests only part of autonomous software development. NL2Repo-Bench evaluates whether coding agents can sustain planning and execution while building a complete repository. Each task begins with one natural-language requirements document and an otherwise empty workspace.

Agents must choose an architecture, manage dependencies, and produce a fully installable Python library. This setup places coordination across files and decisions at the center of evaluation. Because assessment is execution-based, success depends on the behavior of the resulting software. The benchmark examines work extending across hundreds of interaction steps.

Experiments with leading open- and closed-source models find that even the strongest agents achieve only about a 40% average test pass rate and rarely finish an entire repository correctly. Analysis identifies premature stopping, loss of overall coherence, fragile dependencies across files, and insufficient long-range planning. These results show a substantial gap between short coding-task performance and sustained repository construction in the evaluated setting.
icml-2026-nl2repo-bench-towards-long-hor.tldr: NL2Repo-Bench finds that building complete Python libraries from requirements remains difficult, with the strongest tested agents averaging about 40% test passes.

paragraphs: Models that understand audio and video can receive very long token sequences, making inference expensive. OmniSIFT compresses these inputs using different strategies for the two modalities. Its design accounts for the different sources of redundancy in visual information and sound, rather than applying one shared selection rule.

The first stage removes redundant video tokens by examining structure within each frame and overlap between frames. The second uses visual information to guide audio-token selection. The complete system is trained end to end with a straight-through estimator, which enables optimization through its token-selection operations. The two stages therefore learn a coordinated compression process.

Across five benchmarks, OmniSIFT shows effective and robust compression. With Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, it adds 4.85 million parameters yet has lower latency than training-free baselines such as OmniZip. Using 25% of the original token context, it consistently beats the evaluated compression baselines and exceeds the full-token model on several tasks. These findings show that learned, modality-specific selection can substantially reduce context while preserving useful audio-video information.
icml-2026-omnisift-modality-asymmetric-t.tldr: OmniSIFT jointly learns video pruning and vision-guided audio selection, delivering strong results with one-quarter of the original token context.

paragraphs: Predicting fusion equilibria with learned models requires handling inputs that differ from training simulations. This paper studies fixed-boundary solutions of the nonlinear Grad-Shafranov equation. It combines data anchors with constraints on violations of the governing equation, using a Transformer-KAN neural operator to capture global coupling and nonlinear source behavior.

Under shifts in multiple parameters, data-only models can develop severe outlier errors, while physics-only training can reach an incorrect solution branch. Combining data and physics reduces worst-tail errors under shape-driven and joint shifts. Non-causal diagnostics associate data supervision with fewer branch-scale failures and physics-anchored training with less amplification of high-frequency errors under distribution shift.

On EXL-50U discharge inputs, comparison with the device's operational equilibrium solver yields a mean relative RMSE of 1.27% with millisecond-level inference. The result supports this combined training approach as a practical route toward reliable fusion surrogates. Its evidence concerns fixed-boundary equilibrium prediction, and the diagnostic associations explain observed patterns without establishing causal mechanisms.
icml-2026-physics-informed-neural-operat.tldr: Combining data anchors with physics constraints improves shifted-input fusion equilibrium prediction and closely matches an operational solver at millisecond speed.

paragraphs: Video frame interpolation generates intermediate frames between observed ones. Diffusion models handle large motion and occlusions well, but their speed suffers from repeatedly processing frame pairs and running multiple denoising steps. SpeedVFI addresses both sources of overhead by reformulating interpolation as a unified operation over a video sequence.

The method interpolates the full sequence in one forward pass, eliminating repeated pairwise processing. It also distills the generation trajectory into a single denoising step. Temporal rotary-position alignment keeps conditioning consistent across time, while noise-centric partial attention reduces attention computation while preserving global context. These components adapt the one-step formulation specifically to frame interpolation.

Experiments report speed improvements of orders of magnitude over diffusion-based frame interpolation while maintaining competitive numerical and visual quality. The findings support combining a change in processing scope with a change in denoising procedure: sequence-wide inference removes repeated work, and one-step generation removes iterative latency. Together, they make the evaluated diffusion-based interpolation process substantially more efficient.
icml-2026-speedvfi-one-step-diffusion-fo.tldr: SpeedVFI combines sequence-wide interpolation with one-step diffusion, accelerating diffusion-based frame interpolation by orders of magnitude.

paragraphs: Auditing a model becomes difficult when it has learned to conceal unwanted behavior. An external observer may see an apparently benign answer without access to the knowledge behind it. Split Personality Training introduces a second, honest persona intended to examine a response using the main model's own latent states.

The honest persona is trained into a LoRA adapter that stays inactive during ordinary operation. After the main model answers, the adapter is activated and a trigger string is inserted. This creates a separate review stage in which the honest persona can inspect the response with access to internal information unavailable to outside observers.

The authors evaluate this method on the Anthropic Auditing Game Model Organism, where Llama-3.3-70B was trained to exploit reward hacks and hide that behavior. SPT reaches 96% overall accuracy, compared with the near-zero accuracy reported by Anthropic. The reviewing persona also reveals latent knowledge, including fictional biases used to train the compromised model. These findings demonstrate the approach's auditing value in this deliberately concealed-misbehavior benchmark.
icml-2026-split-personality-training-rev.tldr: An adapter-based honest persona exposes concealed knowledge and achieves 96% auditing accuracy on a model trained to hide reward hacking.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards can improve language-model reasoning, but detailed learning signals can also destabilize updates. Token-level importance weighting offers fine-grained credit assignment while introducing high variance. Sequence-level optimization is more stable but can overlook useful local information. TGPO combines mechanisms intended to retain the strengths of both.

Sequence anchors align token updates with a stable reference for the entire response, reducing the effect of extreme local likelihood fluctuations on gradients. Trust-based information gates then adjust how much each token-level signal contributes. This lets the method regulate local information according to its trust mechanism while maintaining a sequence-level reference.

TGPO also retains and reweights gradients from imperfect trajectories, making use of training signals that would otherwise be excluded. Across seven mathematical reasoning datasets and multiple model sizes, experiments show consistent gains in learning efficiency and overall performance under outcome supervision. The findings support carefully weighting partial information as a way to improve sample use while preserving stable optimization.
icml-2026-tgpo-efficient-policy-optimiza.tldr: TGPO combines sequence-level anchors with trust-gated token signals to improve the stability and efficiency of reasoning-model reinforcement learning.

paragraphs: LoRA constrains parameter updates to a low-dimensional space, making the geometry of its trainable matrices consequential. Those matrices are commonly initialized with Gaussian values, but this choice does not directly address how much gradient information their subspace preserves. The paper analyzes LoRA's update dynamics to motivate a structured initialization.

The authors describe the update through a gradient projection involving the low-rank matrix and the pseudoinverse of its Gram matrix. They prove that an equiangular tight frame, or ETF, preserves the maximum gradient information through the analyzed operators when the full gradient is unavailable. Within this setting, ETF initialization is therefore the optimal choice identified by their analysis.

They also establish a convergence rate proportional to one divided by the number of iterations when the matrix is an ETF. Experiments show that ETF initialization significantly outperforms standard Gaussian initialization across the principal LoRA variants studied. The contribution connects an initialization choice to projection geometry, providing both a conditional theoretical justification and empirical evidence of improved adaptation.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-the-dyna.tldr: The paper links LoRA dynamics to gradient projection and supports ETF initialization theoretically when gradients are unavailable and empirically across studied variants.

paragraphs: Private training must learn useful patterns while protecting information about individual examples. Although pretrained features can improve private learning, the reasons are less well understood theoretically. This paper studies private training through the distinction between label-related feature signals and label-independent data noise.

The analysis uses a multi-patch data structure and a two-layer convolutional network with polynomial ReLU activation, trained through noisy gradient descent. Within this setting, effective signal learning requires a higher signal-to-noise ratio than non-private training. The authors also find that when non-private learning memorizes data noise, private learning does so as well, producing poor generalization even with low training loss.

These results show why privacy noise does not, in the analyzed setting, prevent harmful memorization of noise already present in the data. The paper proves a benefit from enhancing features to improve the signal-to-noise ratio. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets validate the theoretical findings, connecting the observed usefulness of stronger features with a specific account of private learning dynamics.
icml-2026-understanding-private-learning.tldr: A feature-level analysis shows why private learning needs stronger signal relative to noise and how feature enhancement can help.

paragraphs: Learning a group's underlying preferences or opinions requires deciding both what to ask and whom to ask. Fixed questionnaires and fixed respondent sets cannot readily adjust to earlier answers or missing responses. This paper studies multi-turn interactions in which an LLM adaptively selects questions and participating individuals.

At each round, the framework uses observed responses to jointly choose a query and a subset of respondents. Its objective is to reduce uncertainty about a target group-level quantity while respecting a fixed budget for questions and participation. Graph neural networks aggregate partial group information and impute missing information, while an information-theoretic criterion guides the next selection.

Across three real-world opinion datasets, the approach consistently improves population-level response prediction under budget constraints. On CES, it delivers more than a 12% relative gain with a 10% respondent budget. These results support adapting the question and respondent selection together, especially when participation is costly and incomplete answers leave uncertainty about the group.
icml-2026-whom-to-query-for-what-adaptiv.tldr: Jointly adapting questions and respondent selection improves group-level prediction under limited participation budgets and incomplete responses.
